# *Need for Speed* (Series)

![NFSUB TeaserBackground](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/nfs/images/8/84/NFSUB_TeaserBackground.gif/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/200?cb=20221006233208&path-prefix=en)

***Need for Speed*** (abbreviation: ***NFS***) is a multiplatform racing video game series with the first game *[The Need for Speed](/wiki/The_Need_for_Speed "The Need for Speed")* being released in December 1994.

On October 21, 2009, [Electronic Arts](/wiki/Electronic_Arts "Electronic Arts") announced the franchise had sold over 100 million units, making *Need for Speed* the most commercially successful racing game series at the time, and 2005's *[Need for Speed: Most Wanted](/wiki/Need_for_Speed:_Most_Wanted_(2005) "Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005)")* being the best selling game in the series with 16 million copies sold.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

## Other[]

### *Need for Speed 64*[]

![NFS64 Fade Art](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)

*Need for Speed 64*[[2]](#cite_note-2), a 64-bit entry in the series for the Nintendo 64 was being developed in 1998 by Paradigm Entertainment alongside [EA Canada](/wiki/EA_Canada "EA Canada").

The project altered during development into *[Beetle Adventure Racing!](https://beetleadventureracing.fandom.com/wiki/ "w:c:beetleadventureracing")* after EA signed a deal with [Volkswagen](/wiki/Volkswagen "Volkswagen") to create a game around the New Beetle[[3]](#cite_note-3) and *HSV Adventure Racing!* in Australia with [Holden Special Vehicles](/wiki/Holden "Holden").

### *Need for Speed: Ferrari*[]

![NFSFR Fade Art](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)

At the beginning of the development of *Porsche Unleashed*, EA was planning to make similar games with different brands, among them Ferrari and BMW. A contract was signed and EA Seattle was counting on developing it as EA Canada would develop the fifth *Need for Speed* game.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

The release of the Ferrari game was cancelled before the release of *Porsche Unleashed*.

### *Need for Speed: Terror 5*[]

![NFST5 Fade Art](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)

*Need for Speed: Terror 5* was a concept for an entry in the *Need for Speed* by [Black Box](/wiki/EA_Black_Box "EA Black Box") and was worked on in 2008.

In a portfolio by Wylie Styles, first published in 2008, the creative goal of the project was for a game depicting "How can large scale street races take place in a post 911 US city?"[[5]](#cite_note-5) The portfolio includes pre-visualisation videos for main menu,[[6]](#cite_note-6) map navigation,[[7]](#cite_note-7)and[[8]](#cite_note-8) TerrorFive access prototypes.

The game would have seen the player participating in underground street racing using a network of smartphones and online surveillance networks turned against the city by a group of racers, ultimately being branded as terrorists by the city and leading to their group being titled "TerrorFive".[[9]](#cite_note-9)

As the player gained a reputation in the racing scene, they would eventually be messaged by TerrorFive and invited to the Underground Racing League as their first step into the group's world.

### *Need for Speed: Millionaire*[]

![NFSMill Fade Art](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)

*Need for Speed: Millionaire* was a concept for an entry in the *Need for Speed* series by [Criterion Games](/wiki/Criterion_Games "Criterion Games") and was worked on it for around six months following the release of *[Need for Speed: Undercover](/wiki/Need_for_Speed:_Undercover "Need for Speed: Undercover")*.[[10]](#cite_note-10)

The concept was revealed by Alex Ward, a long-standing developer at Criterion Games, through a series of Twitter posts in October 2013 and in an interview with Official Xbox Magazine published in their May 2016 issue.[[11]](#cite_note-11)

The game was to be online-only game in which the player would have been a lottery winner and could play with their friends in [challenges](https://topgear.fandom.com/wiki/Cheap_Car_Challenges "w:c:topgear:Cheap Car Challenges") similar to those in the [Top Gear](https://topgear.fandom.com/wiki/Top_Gear "w:c:topgear:Top Gear") television series.[[13]](#cite_note-13)

### *Shift 3*[]

![S3 Fade Art](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)

*Shift 3* is a cancelled sequel to *[Shift 2: Unleashed](/wiki/Shift_2:_Unleashed "Shift 2: Unleashed")* and would have served as a continuation of the series as a spin-off from the *Need for Speed* series.[[14]](#cite_note-14)

Ian Bell, the CEO of Slightly Mad Studios during the development of the *Shift* series, spoke in a live Q&A with SpotTheOzzie on September 19, 2017, a few days prior to the release of *[Project CARS 2](https://projectcars.fandom.com/wiki/Project_CARS_2 "w:c:projectcars:Project CARS 2")*, in a response to question regarding the crowdfunding of *[Project CARS](https://projectcars.fandom.com/wiki/Project_CARS "w:c:projectcars:Project CARS")*.[[15]](#cite_note-15)

### *Need for Speed: Most Wanted 2*[]

![NFSMW2 Fade Art](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIABAAAAAP///yH5BAEAAAEALAAAAAABAAEAQAICTAEAOw%3D%3D)

*Need for Speed: Most Wanted 2* is a cancelled requel being developed by [Criterion Games](/wiki/Criterion_Games "Criterion Games") following the release of [*Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit* (2010)](/wiki/Need_for_Speed:_Hot_Pursuit_(2010) "Need for Speed: Hot Pursuit (2010)").

Hawaii, the project's codename, had a length development period in 2011 with multiple builds featuring a new *Need for Speed: Most Wanted* branding[[17]](#cite_note-17) up until near the end of December 2021, at which point the branding was changed for *Need for Speed: Most Wanted 2*,[[18]](#cite_note-18) but was altered again to another *Need for Speed: Most Wanted* branding in March 2012[[19]](#cite_note-19) before changing again at the end of May 2012 to the branding used for [*Need for Speed: Most Wanted* (2012)](/wiki/Need_for_Speed:_Most_Wanted_(2012) "Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2012)").[[20]](#cite_note-20)

Moodboards[[21]](#cite_note-21) and pre-visualisation videos[[22]](#cite_note-22)[[23]](#cite_note-23) published by an artist working at Criterion during Hawaii's development showcase an initially darker and gritter tone for the game. An internal sizzle reel compiled by Arnson Communications, Inc showcases various gameplay elements of the in-development game.[[24]](#cite_note-24)[[25]](#cite_note-25)
